title: Simulating Flood Insurance in New Orleans
gallery_text: My sandbox simulates how flood insurance coverage could decline as coastal land loss grows in New Orleans. I wanted to test if there was a gap between exposure and insurance, since that pattern had started to appear in assignment 2. I used USGS land-change and FEMA NFIP policy data to project tract-level policy counts under adjustable penalty and protection assumptions through 2045.

answers.process: I feel like when I was building the model it made me realize that there was a gap between what I wanted the result to be and the data. For example, some of the questions that the agent asked me were super helpful to make me realize how the rule I built was working. Like some of the areas had no measurable land loss, or there were other things I was forced to simplify.
answers.result: I feel like the results work a lot better for the simulating policy side than the land loss, since you can barely see the change here. I also wish I made an option in which you could overlay both so you could see the actual difference or gap. The result does feel coherent with the actual conditions and other results I got before. I was also surprised that there were some areas where there was policy growth in some areas.
answers.unexpected: I originally expected insurance coverage to track land loss fairly directly such as more disappearing land, more exposure, more visible response in policy counts. However the results show that policy counts are declining almost everywhere making the question more about where this land loss makes the policy trend loss worse.
